title: More ways to see who is building what
summary:
Community publishers gained profiles, accounts gained an MCP quest tool, eleven apps joined the catalog, and SDK and model requests got less surprising.

Community model publishers can add a public name and service link that appear alongside their models in Enter. The new read-only `listQuests` MCP tool lets an authenticated account check its quests and earned rewards; claiming still happens in the dashboard.

Community additions span batch image generation, jewelry renders from kids’ sketches, cat-photo stickers, Arabic/English story development, no-code agent workflows, and a fortune teller that reads receipts. The additions bring the App Greenhouse to 858 apps.

SDK model listings now return raw registry fields in server order, so consumers handle their own presentation. Convenience helpers make one request and return one result; callers wanting multiple images can use `imageGenerate({ n })`. Unset model and voice options now stay unset, while the API defaults model-free video requests to `veo` and image edits to `flux`. Shared request handling was also simplified across developer tools, and MCP web search now accepts models advertising the capability rather than a fixed list.

highlights.title: Check quests through MCP
highlights.text: Use the read-only `listQuests` tool to see an authenticated account’s quests and earned rewards. Claiming rewards still happens in the dashboard. [Explore MCP servers](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs#tag/mcp-servers).

highlights.title: Profiles for community publishers
highlights.text: Community model publishers can set a public provider name and service link, shown alongside their models in Enter. [Browse models](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models).

highlights.title: More models for MCP search
highlights.text: MCP web search accepts models that advertise `web_search` capability instead of relying on a three-model list. [Explore MCP servers](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs#tag/mcp-servers).
